**Poetic and prophetic:**  
With the shedding of the old, I will step on the head of the serpent, leaving evil behind as God leads me into what’s next.

**Subtle but powerful:**  
As the Year of the Snake ends, I will rise, step on the head of the serpent, and follow God into a new season of freedom.

If you want it more mystical, more scripture-coded, or softer for a broader audience, tell me the vibe and I’ll tune it perfectly.

I’ve been thinking a lot about cycles lately. And about God’s timing.

The Year of the Snake asked me to shed. Not gently. Not politely. God began removing layers I had clung to for safety, approval, and survival. The version of me that stayed silent too long. The version that confused endurance with love. The marriage that slowly taught me to shrink myself to stay safe.

Leaving an abusive narcissist was not just a divorce. It was a death. And God was with me in that valley. When I didn’t have clarity, He did. When I didn’t have strength, He carried me. What felt like loss was actually rescue.

Shedding is holy work. It’s painful. It’s humbling. It’s lonely. But it’s necessary. Scripture talks about pruning for a reason. God removes what is dead or harmful so new life can grow.

Now we’re moving toward the Year of the Fire Horse. A cycle that only comes once every 60 years. Known for movement, courage, and transformation. Fire refines. The Horse moves forward without fear. And I can feel God saying, “It’s time to rise.”

The last time this energy appeared was 1966, when the world began questioning what it had accepted as normal. Old systems cracked. Voices rose. Truth could no longer be buried.

That feels familiar.

For me, this season is resurrection. God is rebuilding me from the ashes like a phoenix, breath by breath. Stronger. Clearer. Whole. I’m building a new business led by purpose, not survival. A life marked by peace, safety, and real love. I’m choosing obedience over fear, faith over familiarity.

This isn’t chaos. It’s alignment. It’s refinement. It’s God lighting the path forward, not destroying me in the fire.

I am no longer the woman who begged for love where God was already offering it freely.

Here’s to the God who rescues, restores, and rebuilds.
Here’s to the fire that refined me.
Here’s to the courage to move when He says go.

From the ashes, by His grace, I rise. 🔥❤️

The Fire Horse only comes around once every 60 years. It’s known as a cycle of movement, courage, and transformation — the kind of energy that doesn’t sit still for long. Fire burns away what isn’t aligned, and the Horse refuses to be contained. When these two come together, change tends to be anything but quiet.

And history reflects that.

The mid-60s weren’t subtle or predictable. They were a turning point. 

People began questioning old systems, challenging authority, and searching for deeper meaning. Culture shifted. Consciousness expanded. 

Humanity, in its own way, started saying, “We’re not doing life the old way anymore.”

Something new began to emerge. Not destruction… but transformation. Not chaos for the sake of chaos… but growth. A clearing. A recalibration. A collective decision to evolve.

Now we’re approaching another Fire Horse cycle in 2026.

Maybe it’s not about expecting the world to fall apart. Maybe it’s about recognizing the quiet momentum already building. People healing. Leaving what no longer fits. Speaking more truth. Creating more heart-centered communities. Choosing alignment over obligation.

Maybe this time we’re not just breaking old structures. Maybe we’re learning how to build something better.

More conscious.
More connected.

If these cycles teach us anything, it’s this: change doesn’t always come to burn everything down. Sometimes it arrives simply to light the way forward. 🔥❤️🔥

---

I’ve been thinking a lot about cycles lately.

The Year of the Snake asked me to shed. Not gently. Not politely. It stripped me of the skin I had outgrown. The version of me that stayed quiet too long. The version that learned to survive instead of live. The marriage that slowly taught me to shrink myself to stay safe. Leaving an abusive narcissist was not just a divorce. It was a death of an old self I no longer recognized or wanted to carry forward.

Shedding isn’t pretty. It’s raw. It’s lonely. It’s terrifying. But it’s necessary.

Now we’re moving toward the Year of the Fire Horse. A cycle that only comes once every 60 years. A force known for movement, courage, and transformation. Fire Horse energy does not linger in the ashes. It rises. It runs. It rebuilds.

The last time this energy appeared was 1966, when the world began questioning everything it had accepted as normal. Old systems cracked. Voices grew louder. People decided they were done living small, quiet, obedient lives.

That feels familiar.

For me, the Fire Horse is about rebuilding myself from the ashes like a phoenix. Stronger. Clearer. More sovereign. It’s about starting a new business rooted in purpose, not survival. Creating a life filled with real love, safety, and truth. Choosing alignment over fear. Expansion over endurance.

This season is not about burning everything down for the sake of destruction. It’s about letting the fire clear what never should have been there in the first place. It’s about movement forward. About momentum. About trusting that what rises after the fire is more powerful than what was lost.

I’m not the woman I was. And I’m deeply grateful for that.

Here’s to the fire that freed me.
Here’s to the horse that carries me forward.
Here’s to a new life built with love, truth, and courage.

From the ashes, I rise. 🔥❤️
